quarterly_data.quarter: Hitachi Energy press release: Hitachi Energy invests $479 million CAD to bring critical (10-16-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Hitachi Energy will invest $479 million CAD (more than $330 million USD) in its North American insulation and components business by building a new Transformer Insulation Factory in London, Ontario, Canada: a planned 21,000-square-meter facility, expected to be completed by 2028, that will manufacture electrical insulation pressboard and laminates for transformers, with Canada's first pressboard manufacturing line and Hitachi Energy's first in the Americas, and over 100 permanent skilled jobs. Support announced: the Government of Canada $20 million CAD through the Strategic Response Fund, the Government of Ontario up to $20 million CAD through the Invest Ontario Fund, and Natural Resources Canada an additional $10 million CAD to Hitachi Energy Canada Inc. The release says transformer manufacturers continue to face global supply constraints, including limited availability of the specialized insulation materials required for transformer production; Helmut Bockshammer (Global Product Group Manager, Insulation & Components): the factory will help address one of the most critical bottlenecks in transformer manufacturing.
quarterly_data.figure: $479 million CAD (more than $330 million USD); 21,000-square-meter facility, completion by 2028; government support $20 million CAD + up to $20 million CAD + $10 million CAD

quarterly_data.quarter: Hitachi Energy press release: Hitachi Energy invests $479 million CAD to bring critical (10-16-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: The London, Ontario facility is part of Hitachi Energy's commitment to invest more than $2 billion USD to bolster the North American supply chain through 2027. Recent Canadian investments named in the release: the acquisition of London-based Canduct, a manufacturer of transformer insulation kits and components, and a $270-million Canadian expansion to nearly triple large power transformer production capacity in Varennes, Quebec.
quarterly_data.figure: more than $2 billion USD through 2027; $270-million Varennes expansion to nearly triple large power transformer capacity
